past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If the current through a coil of an electromagnet reverses, then the
options: C. direction of the magnetic field reverses.
D. direction of the magnetic field remains the same.
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: The direction of the magnetic field produced by an electromagnet depends on the direction of the electric current flowing through its coil (given by the right-hand grip rule). Reversing the current reverses the direction of the magnetic field.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: Electromagnets are commonly used in all of the following electrical instruments EXCEPT
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Toasters use heating elements (resistors) operating on the heating effect of electric current (Joule heating), not electromagnets. Electric irons also use heating elements, while motors and generators rely on electromagnets/magnetic fields.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: Which of the following symbolises of a NAND gate?
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: A NAND gate is represented by an AND gate symbol followed by a small inversion bubble at its output.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: Cathode Rays Oscilloscope (CRO) is NOT used
options: B. to measure alternating and direct currents.
C. to measure the effects of background radiation.
D. to study the effects of electric field on moving charges.
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: A CRO is an electronic test instrument used to display and analyze waveforms (acting as a voltmeter, measuring AC/DC voltages, and studying electric/magnetic fields on moving charges). It is not designed or used to measure background radiation (which requires a Geiger-Muller counter or similar detector).

crqs.question: State Fleming's left-hand rule for the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
crqs.answer: Hold the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the left hand mutually perpendicular: if the Forefinger points in the direction of the Magnetic Field and the Middle finger in the direction of Conventional Current, the Thumb points in the direction of the Magnetic Force (Motion).
crqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-II Model Paper I Q.23

erqs.question: Explain the working principle of a D.C. motor and state four factors that increase the turning effect (magnetic torque) on its armature coil.
erqs.answer: A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences equal and opposite forces on its two sides, forming a couple that rotates the coil; a split-ring commutator reverses current every half turn to maintain continuous rotation. Torque increases with: (1) larger current I, (2) stronger magnetic field B, (3) more turns N, and (4) larger coil area A.

numericals.problem: Why does a soft-iron core placed inside a current-carrying solenoid greatly increase its magnetic field strength, yet lose magnetism immediately when the current is switched off?
numericals.solution: Soft iron has high magnetic permeability so its magnetic domains align rapidly with the solenoid field, and low retentivity so domains randomise as soon as current stops.
